slides.text: **Chatbots** are tools based on artificial intelligence. The word _'intelligence'_ can be misleading – the chat doesn't actually understand us. Why does it answer the questions so accurately so often?

Chatbots cannot speak our language - they can only estimate the **probability** of a word sequence occurring, thanks to previous analysis of massive databases. In other words, they repeat what _most frequently_ appeared in the texts they analyzed.

This means that chatbots are also **limited** to the data and information collected in a given model. The data they base their work on can contain _lies and inaccuracies_ - which should draw our attention.

title: AI as a shortcut in search engines

slides.text: Currently, most search engines are enhanced with an **AI shortcut**. We often find the answer to our burning question there and skip further information searches and analysis of various articles.

Remember that **AI chooses** what is _'most important'_ and at the same time can omit many crucial details. Sometimes the lack of these nuances can lead to a skewed or incorrect interpretation. Moreover, it **does not verify** the page it draws information from - we, as users, must assess whether the source is trustworthy (which we will mention in subsequent lessons).
Perhaps you've seen memes laughing at absurd AI answers. Let us remember that sometimes something that seems **logical** at first glance can also turn out to be **nonsense**.

The AI shortcut _does not always_ show links, _does not always_ quote accurately, and the source of the given information _is not always visible_. **It is you** who should ensure that you can trust the information you see.

Watch out for AI shortcuts, especially if you are looking for **legal**, **medical**, **financial**, or **political** information - obtaining incorrect knowledge on these topics can carry severe consequences.

If you add `-ai` to the end of your search query in a search engine, you will get results without the **AI** summary. This allows you to compare websites without being influenced by the AI's interpretation.

title: AI as a shortcut in search engines
question: Does the AI shortcut in search engines always provide reliable information from verified sources?
options: No, AI does not verify sources and can omit crucial details
Yes, every piece of information provided by AI is fully verified
Yes, but only for medical and legal topics
No, AI shortcuts never provide any useful information
explanation: The AI shortcut in search engines often does not verify source pages and selects selective facts, which is why you must always remain vigilant.

title: How is AI able to create images?

slides.text: Just like when asking a chat questions – answers don't come from a vacuum. **AI image generators** use large collections of existing images from which they _'learn'_ to then generate pictures.
**Risks:** Generators not only create images based on a massive database of existing ones, but they also _imitate artists' styles_.
**Risks:** An image generator **is not an artist**. If it is instructed to create a comic on a given topic, it will use existing works in its database to do so.
**Risks:** Generators are constantly being improved, but they can always have **shortcomings** - especially when generating text on an image or numerous fine details.

title: How is AI able to create images?
question: On what principle do AI-based image generators work?
options: They 'learn' from large collections of existing images and generate new ones based on that
They possess built-in genuine human creativity and paint from scratch
They download random graphics from Google Search and display them unchanged
They draw only geometric shapes and statistical charts
explanation: AI generators need massive collections of training images to learn patterns and styles, which they then imitate.

slides.text: Images created by artificial intelligence make **fake news** more believable. Using `deepfakes`, someone's reputation can be ruined by generating a video with a false statement.
Remember that just as artificial intelligence can be used to create an image, it can also be used to **detect** whether a given image is real or created by AI.
If you suspect that a given image is fake, **do not share it** online. In this way, you will stop **disinformation**.
Most of us share some information about ourselves on the internet. Sometimes we share a photo of a dog on social media, sometimes a received diploma, or a gathering with friends.
Every photo is a **digital footprint**!
However, there are photos that carry a _particular risk_.
